item: The Wikipedia lane keeps its own hourly history, times every tick and drain stage, and reads its hot sets in one pass
status: shipped (fixture-verified; awaiting the operator's next bundle)
key_paths: src/wiki/history.py; src/wiki/hotset.py; src/wiki/runner.py; src/wiki/walk.py; src/wiki/lane_models.py; src/wiki/service.py; src/api/diagnostics/wiki_lane_history.py; tests/test_wiki_lane_history.py; tests/test_wiki_hotset_one_pass.py
summary: Read from the 15 bundles of 2026-10-06: the walk ran at 37 % of its ceiling (559 requests an hour against about 1,500) and nothing in the files said where the rest went, and every drain read the lane's whole entity table once per followed edition (2.3 s of CPU per drain at 200,000 entities, 0.34 s in one pass; same sets, equivalence-tested). New: table wiki_lane_hourly (7 days, in the lane's own file, pruned hourly) holding per hour and edition the walk's requests, answer ms, bytes, pages, refusals by kind with the longest Retry-After, each drain's outcome and its hot-set and feed stages, each tick's seconds in drain, pageviews, index, warm, walk and sleep, and the stream's per-tick counter differences; drain_status gains tick, drain_duration (p50, p95, max and stage totals over the last 10,000 drains) and history; GET /api/diagnostics/wiki-lane-history and the bundle member wiki-lane-history.json carry it whole. Rows are written inside transactions that already exist, so recording adds no commit and a failed flush is counted and never stops the lane. No walk or stream behaviour changed. Gate row F and S05-06 now say a pass costs (articles + redirects) / 50 requests, not articles / 50.
